top_stories.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
top_stories.one_liner: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.
top_stories.summary: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.
top_stories.ai_overview: Combatting adversarial distillation How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry. As frontier AI models become more capable, safeguards play an increasingly important role in how they can be used responsibly.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards.
ai_key_details: An actor may use a frontier model’s outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities, then deploy it without comparable protections.

For instance, an adversary might distill a model’s cyber capabilities and use the resulting model to help carry out cyberattacks that the original model would have refused to assist with or that its safeguards would have blocked.
We’ve strengthened our defenses against protected reasoning extraction in GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol.
The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.
top_stories.ai_why_it_matters: Our consistent-standards policy establishes shared standards for safeguards and coordinated enforcement across providers offering our models.
top_stories.ai_technical_breakdown: We’re sharing how OpenAI detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, how we’ve strengthened protections for our models’ protected reasoning, and what we’ve learned that can help strengthen defenses across the industry.

top_stories.ai_whats_new: After reinforcement learning, the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget tested on both benchmarks shown, while the summary-trained student scored higher at lower budgets.
ai_key_takeaways: Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities.
These updated safeguards align more closely with those we use for biology and cybersecurity.

We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought.

top_stories.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
top_stories.one_liner: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
top_stories.summary: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
top_stories.ai_overview: From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently(opens in a new window), predictor) on a very large corpus of data.1 I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards.
ai_key_details: As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI.

Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared(opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry.
The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5.
GPT‑3.5, at a log-perplexity of ~0.99 on our current main evaluation dataset, was capable of fluent conversation and formed the basis for the original ChatGPT.
top_stories.ai_why_it_matters: Having experienced that allows us to extrapolate—such a sudden transformation is plausible in deep learning research too.
top_stories.ai_technical_breakdown: A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model.

top_stories.ai_whats_new: Setting the new perplexity state-of-the-art on older datasets4, GPT‑2 was arguably the first model capable of consistently formulating coherent paragraphs of text.
ai_key_takeaways: We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts.

Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “an alien mind”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation.

The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset.2, 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions.

top_stories.title: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates?
top_stories.one_liner: MedChemBench evaluates how well AI models interpret molecular structures, reason from experimental evidence, and select compounds in early drug discovery.
top_stories.summary: MedChemBench evaluates how well AI models interpret molecular structures, reason from experimental evidence, and select compounds in early drug discovery.
top_stories.ai_overview: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates? Introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that tests how well AI models read molecular structures, interpret experimental results, and choose which compounds to test next.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: We’re introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that evaluates AI models on reasoning tasks drawn from medicinal chemistry research.
ai_key_details: It tests whether models can connect a molecule’s structure with experimental evidence to explain results, compare compounds, and predict their properties.
Building AI that can reliably support this work is one step towards helping scientists develop better medicines.

top_stories.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
top_stories.one_liner: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.
top_stories.summary: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.
top_stories.ai_overview: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth How Google DeepMind researchers built a new agentic framework that formally verified the code of Signal’s cryptographic protocol — long considered to be a grand security challenge Today, we’re sharing a milestone in software security long considered to be a grand challenge: Google DeepMind researchers guided AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol, the technology that protects billions of private conversations in apps like Signal and Google Messages. This breakthrough discovery was made using AlphaProof Code, a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: Formal verification—mathematically proving code runs correctly without flaws—is the highest standard of security assurance; however, it is difficult and often labor-intensive.
ai_key_details: Our work marks the first time AI has been used to formally verify a widely deployed cryptographic protocol at this depth.
It's also the first time the implementation of a widely deployed protocol like this has been formally verified by any method, with or without AI.
top_stories.ai_why_it_matters: While prior formal verification work has necessarily focused on smaller scopes, this new approach enables a significant expansion.
top_stories.ai_technical_breakdown: How we verified Signal AlphaProof Code is a multi-LLM agentic framework that splits the work of formal verification the way a research team would: human experts work with AI to decide what to prove, and a group of AI agents does it.

top_stories.ai_whats_new: First, our researchers collaborated with a mix of models to translate Signal’s security goals into formal mathematical specifications, with human experts reviewing every one.
ai_key_takeaways: From there, agents powered by Gemini Carbon did the proofs, generating over six million lines of Lean, a computer language that mathematically proves the accuracy of code.
Next, the agents audited the proof and highlighted areas that needed a second look by a human – just one percent of the codebase, a massive time savings.
Because Lean automatically checks the rest, our experts could focus their review where human judgment matters most.
